ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the side length of each small square is 1. What is the degree measure of $\angle ABC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect AC,\\
by the Pythagorean theorem, we have $AC^{2}=2^{2}+1^{2}=5$,\\
$BC^{2}=2^{2}+1^{2}=5$,\\
$AB^{2}=1^{2}+3^{2}=10$,\\
$\therefore AC^{2}+BC^{2}=5+5=10=AB^{2}$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ABC$ is an isosceles right triangle, $\angle ACB=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=\boxed{45^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First read the grid positions from the diagram: taking A as a grid corner, B is 3 unit squares to the right and 1 unit square down from A, while C is 1 unit square to the right and 2 unit squares down from A. Connect AC mentally or on the diagram. From the unit-square text, compute distances by grid offsets: AB^2 = 3^2 + 1^2 = 10, AC^2 = 1^2 + 2^2 = 5, and BC^2 = 2^2 + 1^2 = 5. Since AC^2 + BC^2 = AB^2 and AC = BC, triangle ABC is an isosceles right triangle with the right angle at C. Therefore the two acute angles at A and B are equal, so angle ABC is 45 degrees.
